chunks.arabic_text: لَا نَعْرِفُهُ إِلَّا مِنْ جِهَةِ عَلِيٍّ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ صَاحِبِ الزَّنج، وَمِنْ جِهَةِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ الْبَلَوِيِّ. وَالَّذِي يُحْمَلُ عَلَيْهِ فَسَائِرُهُ فَاسِدٌ.

translations.en: We do not recognize him except from the direction of Ali ibn Muhammad, the Sahib of the Zanj, and from the direction of Abdillah ibn Muhammad al-Balawi. And that which is he is charged with, then the rest of it is corrupt.

en.summary: This entry from al-Ghada'iri's *Kitab al-Du'afa* highlights Muhammad ibn Abdillah al-Ja'fari, whose reliability is assessed primarily through his transmission chains via Ali ibn Muhammad (Sahib al-Zanj) and Abdillah ibn Muhammad al-Balawi. The scholar concludes that the criticisms leveled against him are sound, rendering his narrations *fasid* (corrupt/defective). This reflects the Shia tradition of rigorous *rijal* (narrator criticism) to ensure the authenticity of hadiths transmitted from the Ahl al-Bayt.
en.seo_question: Who is Muhammad ibn Abdillah al-Ja'fari and what is his status in Shia hadith sciences?

key_terms.صَاحِبِ الزَّنج: Sahib of the Zanj (referring to Ali ibn Muhammad, a prominent narrator from the era of the Zanj revolt)
key_terms.الْبَلَوِيِّ: Al-Balawi (a nisba indicating origin from Balas, a region in Khorasan)
key_terms.فَسَائِرُهُ فَاسِدٌ: Then the rest of it is corrupt (indicating the validity of the charges against him affects his overall reliability)
